conflicts.topic: Bulk diffraction versus local incomplete conversion

claims.label: Powder XRD
claims.statement: For 2–3 µm mean Al feed at 1100 °C, both the unmodified and 13 wt% AlCl3 cases show only nano-AlN XRD peaks.

claims.label: TEM / EDX
claims.statement: Both contain spherical aggregates at least 200 nm across built from equiaxed particles at most 20 nm; EDX finds excess Al in these regions.

conflicts.handling: Preserve technique and sampling basis. No complete conversion or phase-pure product is inferred from the XRD-only statement.

claims.statement: Footnote 6 uses 28 nm nano-Al at 0.5 mol% catalyst, while the Kelvin discussion uses a 44 nm coherence length.

conflicts.handling: Retain separate contexts and unresolved batch identities; do not repair, average or infer a complete catalyst–size mapping.

source_interpretation.text: The authors link the greater reactivity of nano-Al to its high surface area. Nano-Al converts fully under their 1000–1100 °C conditions, while coarse commercial feedstocks retain local excess Al even when powder XRD shows only AlN reflections. The smaller feedstock does not imply that its original size survives: partially reacted Al/AlN droplets are 5–15 µm.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Nitridation, footnote 11 and partial-reaction discussion

source_interpretation.topic: AlCl3 as a proposed vapor-transport reagent
source_interpretation.text: AlCl3 addition favors whisker growth and changes partially reacted droplet shapes. The proposed Figure 2 transport cycle involves volatile AlCl and AlCl3, with AlN deposition from vapor. These transient species and reaction pathways are proposed from morphology and cited equilibria, not directly measured intermediates.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 2 and vapor-transport discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Heating rate changes the reaction history
source_interpretation.text: Rapid heating is proposed to reduce the time available for Al particles to coalesce and for AlCl3 to sublime away before nitridation begins. The source places reaction onset around 1073 K, about 140 K above Al melting. This mechanistic onset is not a new specimen-specific synthesis schedule.

source_interpretation.topic: Why the authors favor vapor–solid growth
source_interpretation.text: No flux droplets were seen at whisker tips, unspecified potential flux materials did not promote whiskers, and diverse branching directions were observed. These observations favor the authors’ vapor–solid interpretation over vapor–liquid–solid growth; they do not identify every unseen intermediate or provide a tested list of flux reagents.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Whisker-growth mechanism discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Measured geometry, a model input and size ranges
source_interpretation.text: The 40–180 nm Scherrer range, 10–200 nm TEM crystallites and 0.5–5 µm aggregates describe different bases in the nano-Al series. Footnote 6 separately labels a 28 nm analytical input. A 44 nm input appears in a Kelvin-equation argument predicting only a 2–3% equilibrium vapor-pressure increase; it is not a new synthetic specimen. The authors instead propose enhanced nonequilibrium steady-state vapor pressure.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Nano-Al characterization, footnote 6 and Kelvin discussion

source_interpretation.text: SAD establishes single crystallinity for the examined whiskers; study-wide whisker diameters are generally 20–100 nm with aspect ratios 20 to greater than 100. SEM alone cannot establish whether the stubble on partially nitrided Al droplets is single-crystal whiskers. TEM fragments show that some similar material is polycrystalline fibers. These observations remain separate rather than relabeling all fibers as whiskers.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Whisker dimensions, partial-reaction discussion and footnote 14

source_interpretation.text: The paper demonstrates morphological control by varying feed size, chloride addition and ramp rate. It does not measure device, thermal, optical or mechanical performance of the resulting particles. The precursor preparation also has a source-reported explosion warning; the referenced six-page SI with detailed precautions and synthetic procedures remains unreviewed.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Introduction, conclusion, footnote 5 and supporting-information notice

general_nanoal_nitridation_structure.scope: Study-wide statement preceding the morphology comparisons. Not a separate measurement of the pure-feed 20 °C/min Figure 1b specimen, and not an assigned per-temperature distribution.
